entradas.titulo: Ownership, move, Copy, clone, and drop
entradas.resumo: Three ownership rules; assignment moves (or copies, if Copy); drop at scope exit; clone is an explicit copy.
One &mut OR several &; a reference lives from its start to its last use; E0499/E0502/E0596.
A slice references a contiguous sequence without owning it; &str as a parameter accepts String, &String, and literals.
Annotations describe relationships, they do not change how long a reference lives; choose the parameter the return value depends on.
Three deterministic rules; if a reference is left without a lifetime, the compiler reports an error.

entradas.titulo: The 'static lifetime and the T: 'static bound
entradas.resumo: A 'static reference lives for the whole program; T: 'static means no non-static references.
Expected failure: Result; contract violation: documented panic!; unwrap/expect in tests, prototypes, or with an explained invariant.
? unwraps the Ok or returns the Err converting via From; only in a function with a compatible return type.
Box<dyn Error> for prototypes; a custom enum with Display, Error, and From when the caller needs to distinguish causes.
Option replaces null; the compiler forces you to handle absence.

entradas.titulo: Structs, enums, newtype, and type alias
entradas.resumo: Enum for exclusive alternatives; struct for parts that coexist; newtype for type safety at no cost.

entradas.titulo: Pattern matching, match, if let, let...else
entradas.resumo: match is exhaustive; let and parameters require irrefutable patterns; a guard does not count toward exhaustiveness.
Generics cost nothing at runtime (monomorphization); traits move the missing-method error to compile time.

onde.secao: Tree: enum, generic or trait object?

entradas.resumo: Trait object for heterogeneous/open collections, at the cost of dynamic dispatch; generic when there is a single concrete type.
The Reference's dispatch rules; the error code E0038 does not appear in the sources.
impl Trait in return position requires a single concrete type; in argument position it is an anonymous generic.
A trait can only be implemented for a type if one of the two is local; newtype works around it.
The Fn* trait depends on what the body does with what it captures; move transfers ownership.
Iterators are lazy; adapters produce another iterator, consumers exhaust it; performance equivalent to loops.
Box puts data on the heap with a single owner; required for recursive types.
Rc: several owners in one thread; RefCell checks borrows at runtime; Rc<RefCell<T>> combines them.

entradas.resumo: Rc cycles leak without any error; Weak breaks the cycle and upgrade returns an Option.

std uses 1:1 threads; the end of main terminates the others; move is required for capture.
send takes ownership of the value; recv blocks; multiple producers clone the Sender.
Arc<Mutex<T>> for state shared between threads; deadlock is still possible.
Markers for transferable ownership and shared access between threads; Rc is not Send.
Futures are lazy; await is the switch point; main cannot be async without a runtime.

entradas.resumo: cargo check is faster than build; release for delivery and benchmarks; clippy/rustfmt/cargo fix come with Rust.

One Cargo.lock and one target for several crates; dependencies between members by path.

Debug: panic on overflow; release: wrap; choose wrapping_/checked_/saturating_/overflowing_ consciously.
A String is not indexed by integer; think in bytes, chars, and grapheme clusters.

UTF-8 source; strict/reserved/weak keywords; r# raw identifiers; escapes per literal type.

entradas.titulo: OOP, inheritance, and the state pattern
entradas.resumo: No implementation inheritance; polymorphism via traits; state pattern with Option<Box<dyn State>> or typestate.
Coercion only at coercion sites; &mut T -> &T works, never the reverse.
A release every six weeks via the train model; only the latest stable is supported.

limites.nota: Choosing and using third-party crates and specific async runtimes are out of scope; the Book only mentions rand (p.30) and trpl/tokio/futures as support (Book p.491, 495, 518) and RBE mentions clap in passing (RBE p.130, 230, 323; version 2.27.1 in RBE p.130 is [DATED]).

The Book only mentions std::sync::atomic as an alternative to Mutex for simple numbers (Book p.482); the Reference uses AtomicUsize/fetch_add only in a static example (Ref p.143). The API and the orderings are [extrapolation].
The Reference treats no_std only in the context of preludes and linking (Ref p.519-527, 569-575); the Book and RBE do not cover embedded development.
The Book only provides a loop vs iterator benchmark (Book p.381) and says test benchmarks require nightly (Book p.278); there is no performance guide.
Cross-compilation and WebAssembly are not addressed in the sources.
The web ecosystem is out of scope; the Book only builds a minimal TCP/HTTP server (Book p.647-689).
Other languages: out of scope for this agent; redirect to the agent for that language.
Infrastructure and databases are outside this agent's sources.
Cited only by name (Rust API Guidelines: Book p.172; Rustonomicon: Ref p.624 and Book p.191) or absent (E0038, cargo audit); the content of these documents is not part of the sources.
